passages.heading: Debt note
passages.text: Note 8 – Credit Facilities and Short-term Borrowings As of December 31, 2025, the Company had credit facilities of RMB 10,495 million (approximately $ 1,502 million), comprised of onshore credit facilities in the aggregate amount of RMB 7,700 million (approximately $ 1,102 million), offshore credit facilities in the aggregate amount of $ 200 million and a credit facility of $ 200 million that can be used for either onshore or offshore. The credit facilities had remaining terms ranging from less than one year to three years as of December 31, 2025 . Our credit facilities mainly include term loans, overdrafts, letters of credit, banker’s acceptance notes and bank guarantees. The credit facilities in general bear interest based on the Loan Prime Rate (“LPR”) published by the National Interbank Funding Centre of the PRC, or Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Each credit facility contains a cross-default provision whereby our failure to make any payment on a principal amount from any credit facility will constitute a default on other credit facilities. Some of the credit facilities contain covenants limiting, among other things, certain additional indebtedness and liens, and certain other transactions specified in the respective agreements. As of December 31, 2025 and 2024 , we had outstanding short-term bank borrowings of $ 30 million and $ 127 million, respectively, mainly to manage working capital at our operating subsidiaries. The RMB denominated bank borrowings bear a weighted-average interest rate of 1.5 % and 1.7 % for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 , respectively, and are due within one year from their issuance dates. As of December 31, 2025 , we also had outstanding bank guarantees of RMB 296 million (approximately $ 42 million) mainly to secure our lease payments to landlords for certain Company-owned restaurants, as well as outstanding bank guarantees of RMB 360 million (approximately $ 52 million) to secure the balance of prepaid stored-value cards issued by the Company pursuant to regulatory requirements. Our credit facilities were therefore reduced by outstanding short-term bank borrowings, adjusted for unamortized interest and collateral, and outstanding guarantees. As of December 31, 2025 , the Company had unused credit facilities of approximately $ 1,378 million.

passages.text: Financial Condition and Results of Operations. The following Management’s Discussion and Analysis (“MD&A”) should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8, the “Forward-Looking Statements” section at the beginning of this Form 10-K and the “Risk Factors” section set forth in Item 1A. All Note references in this MD&A refer to the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements included in Item 8. of this Form 10-K. Tabular amounts are displayed in millions of U.S. dollars except per share and unit count amounts, or as otherwise specifically identified. Percentages may not recompute due to rounding. Throughout this Form 10-K when we refer to the “financial statements,” we are referring to the “Consolidated Financial Statements,” unless the context indicates otherwise. This MD&A includes a discussion of our results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. For a discussion of our operating results for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, please refer to Part II, Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024. Overview Yum China Holdings, Inc. is the largest restaurant company in China in terms of 2025 system sales, with $11.8 billion of revenues in 2025 and 18,101 restaurants as of year-end 2025. Our growing restaurant network consists of our flagship KFC and Pizza Hut brands, as well as emerging brands such as Lavazza, Huang Ji Huang, Little Sheep and Taco Bell. We have the exclusive right to operate and sublicense the KFC, Pizza Hut and, subject to the agreed terms, Taco Bell brands in China (excluding Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan) and own the intellectual property of the Little Sheep and Huang Ji Huang concepts outright. We also established a joint venture with Lavazza Group, the world-renowned family-owned Italian coffee company, to explore and develop the Lavazza coffee concept in China. KFC was the first major global restaurant brand to enter China in 1987. With more than three decades of operations, we have developed extensive operating experience in the China market. We have since grown to become the largest restaurant company in China in terms of 2025 system sales, with 18,101 restaurants covering over 2,500 cities primarily in China as of December 31, 2025. We believe that there are significant opportunities to further expand within China, and we intend to focus our efforts on increasing our geographic footprint in both existing and new cities. KFC is the leading and the largest quick-service restaurant (“QSR”) brand in China in terms of system sales. As of December 31, 2025, KFC operated 12,997 restaurants in over 2,500 cities across China. Pizza Hut is the leading and the largest casual dining restaurant (“CDR”) brand in China in terms of system sales and number of restaurants. As of December 31, 2025, Pizza Hut operated 4,168 restaurants in over 1,000 cities. We have two reportable segments: KFC and Pizza Hut. credit_strengths.text: Yum China's operating cash flow comfortably exceeds capital spending, leaving substantial free cash flow after funding its restaurant network expansion. This internally generated liquidity, rather than borrowed money, finances the growth of KFC and Pizza Hut outlets across Chinese cities, supporting a self-funding model that reduces reliance on external refinancing.

The balance sheet carries a net cash position, with unrestricted cash exceeding reported interest-bearing borrowings. Leverage sits far below the consumer discretionary sector median, and the indicative financial risk profile is minimal. This provides a meaningful buffer against cyclical restaurant demand and input-cost volatility.

key_risks.text: The debt note discloses cross-default provisions across credit facilities, so a payment failure on any single facility could trigger defaults on others. Covenants also restrict additional indebtedness and liens. With unused facilities available, this structural feature concentrates refinancing and compliance risk even though drawn borrowings are currently modest.

Disclosed forward-looking statements flag that capital-return plans, including buybacks and dividends, depend on market conditions and capital needs. Shareholder distributions materially exceed free cash flow, so sustained payouts could require drawing on cash reserves or credit facilities, weakening the currently strong liquidity position if operating cash flow softens.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow covers reported borrowings many times over, and the current ratio is near parity, indicating adequate near-term liquidity. However, interest expense is not separately tagged in the available data, so interest coverage cannot be measured directly. This gap is material because it prevents a full assessment of fixed-charge obligations.

Reported short-term borrowings declined sharply year over year, and the debt note shows outstanding bank borrowings are due within one year from issuance. The maturity profile is therefore short but small relative to cash and unused credit facilities, so refinancing risk appears manageable under current conditions.

overall_credit_view.text: Yum China presents a minimal indicative financial risk profile, with net cash, strong free cash flow conversion and leverage well below the sector median. Operating margins are thinner than the sector median, reflecting the competitive restaurant landscape, but cash generation and balance-sheet strength offset this profitability gap.

Analyst judgement: the credit should remain resilient given net cash and substantial unused facilities, though heavy shareholder distributions and short-dated borrowings warrant monitoring. The absence of disclosed interest expense limits precise coverage analysis, and the partial debt sum excludes long-term borrowings, so total debt may be understated.

credit_strengths.text: 百勝中國的營運現金流穩健地超過資本開支，在為其餐廳網絡擴張提供資金後仍留下大量自由現金流。此內部產生的流動性，而非借入資金，為肯德基和必勝客在中國各城市門店的增長提供資金，支持一種減少依賴外部再融資的自給自足模式。
資產負債表持有淨現金狀況，未受限現金超過所報告的計息借款。槓桿遠低於非必需消費品行業中位數，指示性財務風險狀況為極低。這為應對週期性餐廳需求及投入成本波動提供了有意義的緩衝。

key_risks.text: 債務票據披露了各信貸融資之間的交叉違約條款，因此任何單一融資的付款違約可能觸發其他融資的違約。契約亦限制額外債務及留置權。由於有未使用的融資額度可用，此結構性特徵集中了再融資及合規風險，儘管目前已提取借款規模不大。
所披露的前瞻性陳述表明，包括回購和股息在內的資本回報計劃取決於市場狀況及資本需求。股東分派大幅超過自由現金流，因此持續派發可能需要動用現金儲備或信貸融資，若營運現金流減弱，將削弱目前強勁的流動性狀況。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流覆蓋所報告借款的倍數極高，且流動比率接近持平，表明近期流動性充足。然而，現有數據中利息費用並未單獨標記，因此無法直接衡量利息覆蓋率。此缺口屬重大，因其阻礙了對固定費用義務的全面評估。
所報告的短期借款同比大幅下降，且債務票據顯示未償還銀行借款自發行日起一年內到期。因此到期結構較短，但相對於現金及未使用信貸融資而言規模較小，故在當前情況下再融資風險似乎可控。

overall_credit_view.text: 百勝中國呈現極低的指示性財務風險狀況，擁有淨現金、強勁的自由現金流轉換及遠低於行業中位數的槓桿。營運利潤率低於行業中位數，反映競爭激烈的餐廳環境，但現金產生及資產負債表實力抵銷了此盈利能力差距。
分析師判斷：鑑於淨現金及大量未使用融資，該信貸應保持韌性，儘管沉重的股東分派及短期借款值得監控。未披露利息費用限制了精確的覆蓋率分析，且部分債務總和排除了長期借款，因此總債務可能被低估。
